comments.content: `is_subclass_of($value::class, \UnitEnum::class)` returns false when `$value::class` is exactly `\UnitEnum` or `\BackedEnum`, but those are interfaces and cannot be instantiated, so this is fine in practice. However, `is_subclass_of` with a string class name and an interface works, but note that `is_subclass_of` will also trigger autoloading. Since `$value` is already an object, `$value instanceof \UnitEnum` would be simpler, faster, and avoid the extra string-based check. Consider using `$value instanceof \UnitEnum`.
